en: As for the seriousness with which the old constitution was taken, so much follows from the course of events that what the assembly was concerned with was not merely the prop which it found for itself in public opinion through that magic formula; according to the majority it professed to maintain its seriousness about that constitution in perpetuity, and it made the demand to be acknowledged as the principal point, namely that the formal principle of law should be acknowledged.

The spirit of formalism and particularity has, as is well known, from time immemorial constituted the character and the misfortune of Germany in history; this spirit has here displayed itself in its full strength.
If one wishes to call it German-ness, then nothing could have been more German than the disposition of the old Württemberg deputies, the nobility included.

But if one understands by German-ness something general and rational according to its concept - amid all the difference of the territorial lordships -, then it will be difficult to find anything more un-German than that disposition.
zh: 至于对那部旧宪法的认真程度，从这一进程的追索中便可看出这么多：等级会议所图的并不只是它借那句魔法公式在舆论中为自己找到的支撑；按多数人的说法，它宣称自己将长久保持对那部宪法的认真态度，并特别把「形式法原则应得到承认」这一要求置于首要地位。
众所周知，形式主义与特殊性的精神一向造就了德国在历史中的性格与不幸；这种精神在这里显出了它全部的力量。
若要把它称作德意志性，那么没有什么能比老符腾堡议员——连贵族包括在内——的心态更德意志的了。
但若人们把德意志性理解为按其概念而言是普遍而合理的东西——尽管各领地的统治权互有差异——那么就很难找到比那种心态更不德意志的东西了。

en: But the immediate consequence of the position which the assembly of the estates gave itself, in that it rejected, set aside, ignored the royal constitution, was that it made itself incapable of an organic activity.

It set itself directly opposite the government, did not form an opposition within a common ground, and removed itself from the relation in which it would have been able to undertake and accomplish effective works on state institutions.

When, after the lapse of three months and a vain waiting for something flourishing to come to light, the patience of a newly Württemberg representative, Mr Gleich of Aalen, finally broke, and he reproached the assembly (Abt. VIII, S. 20 f.) among other things with occupying itself almost always only with secondary matters and leaving the main thing out of sight, this was declared to him to be quite wrong, for the assembly had resolved in one sitting that every member should be called upon to prepare himself on a draft of the charter of the constitution! - As if every deputy had not already had to bring his whole preparation with him, and as if such a resolution of the assembly, that every member should prepare himself, had been a piece of work and an answer, when after three months of work by an assembly one is asked. - In any case one has seen above that on the 26 October following the assembly realised that it was impossible for it to communicate the fundamental laws of its constitution, because it had not yet been able to use the land archive.
zh: 然而，等级会议既然抛弃、撇开、无视了王家的宪法，它给自己采取的这一立场的直接后果就是：它使自己不能从事任何有机的生命活动。
它直接站到了政府的对面，没有在一个共同的基础之内形成反对派，并自行退出了那种能够就国家机构进行有效工作并使之得以实现的关系。

当新符腾堡的代表阿伦的格莱希先生，在三个月过去、而某种兴旺之事迟迟不见踪影地徒然等候之后，终于失去了耐心，并就其他事情之外指责等级会议（《文件补编》 VIII, S. 20 f.）几乎总是只忙于旁枝末节而把主要之事丢在脑后时——这一点向他宣称是完全错误的，因为等级会议曾在一次会议中作出决议：要求每一位成员都就一份宪章文书的草案作好准备！——仿佛每一位议员不是早已该把自己的全部准备带在身来似的；又仿佛等级会议关于每位成员都应作准备这样一个决议，在人们询问一个等级会议三个月的工作成果时，就算是一项工作、一个答复似的。——此外，人们上面已经看到，在紧接着的 10 月 26 日，等级会议才想到，要陈述其宪章的基本法条是不可能的，因为它还不能利用土地档案馆。

en: The estates were therefore not indeed inactive, but on their diplomatic path they have done enough of their formal business.

But since that business is entirely confined within the conditional limits of a merely positive standpoint - a standpoint which, even as a positive one, no longer has any reality -, the more lively the interest in the assertion of formal law becomes, the less an independent rational content presents itself; and in this exposition, which has already touched upon the most important points, the course of history, moreover known to the public, can only be carried further with reference to its main moments.
zh: 因此等级议会固然并非无所作为，而是在它们的外交途径上把形式上的事务办得够多了。
但这件事既然完全被限制在一种纯粹实证立场的有限界限之内——而这种立场即便作为实证的立场也已不再有任何现实性——那么，对形式法的主张越是热心，所呈现出来的独立理性内容就越少；而在这一已经触及最重要观点的叙述中，那条公众早已知晓的历史进程，也只能就其主要环节再作追述。

en: To the first representation of the estates mentioned above, in which they had declared the rejection of the royal constitution in a delicate manner - properly speaking, however, in a manner that was not open and frank, but was to be concealed and scribbling -, the king replied two days later simply by referring them to the rights appertaining to them by virtue of this constitution, and reminding them that in this respect, if they wished to bring forward individual wishes, the way to doing so was opened to them; there was added the assurance that such wishes and petitions would find a gracious hearing as soon as the king should acquire the conviction that they were in accordance with the interest of the entire kingdom.
zh: 对于上面提到的等级议会第一次呈递的陈述——他们在其中以一种微妙的、其实并非公开坦率、而是要加以隐藏的潦草涂写的方式宣告了对王家宪法的扬弃——国王两天以后就简单地把他们指回依这部宪法属于他们的权利，并提醒他们：在这一方面，如果他们要提出个别愿望，通往此道的门已经为他们打开；同时附上了这样的保证：这样的愿望与请求，只要国王确信它们符合整个王国的利益，就必将得到恩准的听取。

en: What more and other answer could the king make to their obscure declaration? - The king demanded things which they should lay before him; in their reply of 23. March they remained at what is insubstantial and formal.

A more detailed draft of a representation, composed by Mr Bolley, in which indeed at the very outset the declaration is made that the estates refrain from entering into a complete examination of the new charter, but which yet brought forward remarks against many of its points, they held back; it should, however, serve as the charter of their political confession of faith and as the account of the reasons for their conduct, and, if necessary, be laid before the royal state ministry in due time (I. Abt., S. 67).

Nothing would indeed have been more necessary than to lay before the ministry the reasons for which they could not accept the royal charter, and above all to enter into a complete examination of it. - Nor are they remarks whose laying before the ministry could advance the matter; to remarks one makes counter-remarks.

The so-called diplomatic path, entered upon in this manner and leading to whatever results it may, also brings with it this: that the parties negotiating lay before each other reasons and counter-reasons.

Moreover, that it is not the relation of government to subject - a relation into which, to be sure, the standesherren first declared they had to enter - it is something quite other than what the principal activity of an assembly of the estates ought to be: examinations and discussions within itself about its subjects. - One may form the thought that, if the state ministers, as is contained in § 26 of the royal charter, had already begun to attend the sittings and to take the floor, the negotiations would perhaps from the outset have been given a different form.

Counter-remarks, refutations, expositions of reasons could not enter into the style of royal rescripts, could not become essays against essays, but [they could be] the content of oral deliverances of the ministers or state councillors in the sittings of the estates.
These too could be brought to examination, indeed to explication and discussion, and possibly be torn out of the muteness and paper-negotiation indicated above.
zh: 国王对他们含糊不清的声明还能作出什么别的答复呢？——国王要求他们把实质性的东西呈交给他；可他们在 3 月 23. 日的答复中仍旧停留在无内容的与形式的层面上。
一份更为详尽的呈递草案由博莱先生起草，其中固然一开始就声明等级议会不打算对新的文书作全面的审查，却仍然对其中许多点提出了异议——他们扣下了这份草案；它本应作为他们政治信念的文书以及他们行为举止之理由的交代，并在必要时适时呈交王家国务部（《文件补编》 I, S. 67）。
确实没有什么比把那些使他们无法接受王家文书的理由呈交各部更为必要的了，尤其是要着手对这部文书作全面的审查。——而且，这些也不是那种呈交给各部就能推进事情的评注；对评注，人们总是要作出反评注。
这条所谓的外交途径，既是这样被开辟起来的、并且会产生出它所能产生的结果，那么它通常还带来这一点：谈判的各方会把理由与反理由摆到对方面前。
而且，它并不是政府与臣民之间的关系——那固然是等级领主们声称首先必须进入的关系——它完全不是等级会议的主要活动所应当是的东西：在其内部就其事务所作的审查与讨论。——人们可以设想：倘若国务大臣们——如王家文书 § 26 所载——当时已经开始出席各次会议并取得发言权，那么这些谈判也许从一开始就会获得另一种形式。
反评注、反驳、对理由的阐述不可能进入王家敕令的文体，也不可能变成以文章对抗文章，而只能是部长或国务顾问在等级会议各次会议中口头陈述的内容。
这些同样可以引向审查，进而引向展开与讨论，并且有可能从上面所指的沉默与纸上交涉之中被拽出来。

en: The representation of the estates of 22. March, by Count von Waldek, repeated the sought-for turn which was neither open nor intelligible: in its concluding plea to leave out the direct demand of the old constitution and to presuppose it instead.

If such a turn could indeed seem worthy and courageous, to make something not at all the subject of a plea and to keep all appearance of doubtfulness far away, this could lead to nothing; the matter had to come to direct speech after all, only later. - The concluding plea therefore, in a more refined way, only went so far as to wish that the king would consent to the extension of the constitution of the hereditary lands to the entire kingdom, and for this purpose there was appended a deduction of the legal claims of the incorporated parts of the country with reference to the hereditary-land constitution. - Further, after the royal resolution had demanded of the estates a statement of their further wishes, they turned this about and wanted to shove it onto the government, to make the beginning with such a statement.

In the entanglements of private business, in the practice of the advocate it may belong to the shrewd rules to keep oneself closed, not to speak first, to wait for the other to come and see, to shift it onto him, to come forward first with one's claims and means; one keeps the advantage of being able to proceed by way of attack, without committing oneself to anything and without exposing oneself, and so forth.

But an assembly of the estates must least of all take its shrewdness from the practice of the advocate. - Instead of giving their wishes on articles of the royal charter, they added a second refined plea - that a statement be made of those modifications which the present circumstances demand, with a view to the reaching of some common agreement -, as if there were no longer anything else in question. - If one does not want to take such assurance and such a plea for mockery, where must it appear but as incomprehensible obtuseness, into which not a single ray of reflection on the position of the opposite party falls, and which goes comfortably on its way without any thought that, in order to bring about an agreement, regard must also in truth be had for the view and the will of that with whom it is to be concluded, and who is indeed the prince and the government.
zh: 3 月 22. 日等级议会的呈递，由瓦尔德克伯爵先生起草，重复了那个既不明朗也不可理解的转折：它在结语中请求撇开对旧宪法的直接要求，而预先设定这部宪法。

如果这样的转折看上去确实既庄重又勇敢——把某件事根本不作请求的对象、并把一切可疑的样子远远排除——那么这不可能导向任何结果；事情终究还是得、只是要晚些、进入直接的语言。——因此结语只是更精细地说到这一点：希望国王同意把世袭领地的宪法扩展到整个王国；为此还附上了一段推演，说明被并入的各部分在世袭领地宪法上的法权要求。——此外，在国王的决议要求等级议会陈述其进一步愿望之后，他们把这一点倒转过来，想把它推给政府，要由政府以此作为开端。
在私人事务的纠葛中、在律师的实务里，保持缄默、不先开口、等对方来看、把事情推给对方、先亮出自己的要求与手段，或许算得上一条精明之策；这样人便保留了主动进攻的好处，既不让自己有所亏欠，也不让自己陷于难堪，等等。

然而，等级会议最不应该从律师的实务中取来它的精明。——他们不去就王家文书的各条陈述自己的愿望，却加上了第二个精细的请求——要求陈述当前情势所要求的那几项修改，以便达成某种共同的协议——仿佛此外再没有什么可谈的了。——如果人们不愿把这样一种确信和这样一个请求当作嘲笑，那么它除了表现为不可理解的迟钝之外还能表现为什么呢——这种迟钝里没有一道反思的光芒落向对立一方的处境，它只是心平气和地继续走自己的路，全然不想：为了达成一项协议，事实上也必须顾及到与之达成协议者的看法与意志，而这位达成协议者甚至就是君主与政府。

en: Thereupon the ministry declared on 4 April that the king had resolved to postpone the detailed reply to this representation until the return of the crown prince and until taking counsel with him.
However, on 17 April the king let a further answer reach the estates at the time when he called on them at the same time to cooperate in raising the extraordinary demands of war.

In it the point of view from which the royal constitution proceeded is set before the eyes, namely: 'given the independence of the state from a superior, the relations between the head of the state and the estates have been determined after the example of other independent states, as has been judged necessary for the establishment of a durable condition, for the safeguarding of the rights of the people, and for the firmness and vigour of the state government, - irrespective of whether the rights of the estates under the former imperial-territorial constitution of the Duchy of Württemberg were more extensive or more restricted; as indeed they are in reality in the new constitution in several essential points, particularly with regard to independence in the estates' deliberations, participation in legislation, and even taxation, which in everything which the imperial and district relations brought with them was not dependent on the consent of the estates, greater than they were in the formerly existing one'.
zh: 各部于是于 4 月 4 日声明：国王已决定，把对这份呈递的详细答复推迟到皇太子归来并与之商议之后。
然而在 4 月 17 日，国王在同时召集等级议会协助筹措战时的非常支出之际，又给等级议会送去了进一步的答复。

其中把王家宪法所由出发的观点摆在眼前，即：「在国家不依赖于任何更高者的独立之下，国家元首与等级之间的关系，是按照其他独立国家的范例而规定的——正如为了奠定一种持久的状态、保障人民的权利以及为了国家政府的稳固与精力所被认为必要的那样——而不问在符腾堡公国旧有的帝国领土宪法之下等级议会的权利是更广还是更受限制；事实上，在新宪法中，就等级审议中的独立、对立法的参与，甚至就赋税——凡帝国与各圈关系所带来的事务，赋税都不依赖等级议会的同意——而言，在若干实质性的点上，这些权利比先前存在的更大。」

en: Further, the king declares that, with a view to achieving a mutual understanding about the applicability of the motions, he will have oral negotiations opened by plenipotentiaries from both sides.
zh: 此外，国王声明，为就各项提案的适用性达成共同的谅解，他将让双方各自的全权代表开始进行口头谈判。

en: The estates, as stated above, made their cooperation in raising the extraordinary demands dependent on the concession of their demands.
They saw the immediate means in a state loan; the obtaining of such a loan on advantageous terms would doubtless have been of importance as a guarantee from the estates.

Here was the moment to be ready, in the words which they were giving utterance to, to sacrifice goods and life for the fatherland and to prove the truth of their good will, - a proof which can only be given by deeds. - This proof by deeds would at the same time have been able to be an introduction to an understanding in general and, more closely, to the establishment of a common debt-redemption fund.

But they did not offer this guarantee; rather, on 18 April they sent the king a few of the essays which they had in stock, repeated their monotonous representations, and then declared themselves ready, on their side, to proceed to the election of plenipotentiaries.
zh: 如上文所述，等级议会把他们在筹措非常支出方面的参与，取决于自己的要求能得到让步。
他们把直接的手段看作一笔国家公债；以优惠的条件取得这样一笔公债，无疑会是一份来自等级议会的保证而具有重大意义。
这里正是那个时刻：在他们说出口的那些话里，他们本可以准备为祖国献出财产与性命，以证明其善意的真实——而这样的证明只能以行动来给出。——这种实践性的证明同时本可以成为走向一种谅解的开端，并且更切近地成为建立共同的债务清偿基金的开端。
然而他们并不提供这种保证，而是在 4 月 18 日把他们手头存有的几篇文章送给国王，重复他们那些单调的陈述，随后声明，他们方面也准备着手选出全权代表。

en: The assembly appointed on 24 April a committee of 25 members, who were to prepare the negotiations, and four commissioners to negotiate with the four state councillors appointed by the king for this purpose, who, as far as one can recall, all seem to have been old Württembergers.
Now a closer introduction seemed to have taken place, which gave hope of leading to the substance.

It soon showed that the committee understood the assigned preparation to mean the direction of the negotiations and the instruction of the estates' negotiating commissioners; that it began its activity in this sense and had de facto taken full power over the negotiations, excluding the assembly itself.

Upon the remark of a member in the assembly on 28 April that the position of the committee should be stated more precisely, Mr Amtsschreiber Bolley, one of the most active members of the committee, assured it that it would take no dangerous steps and would, where necessary, communicate with the assembly of the estates; in negotiations certain things had to be kept secret.

Upon this assurance the assembly formally transferred to the committee the direction of the negotiations, with the ratification of the assembly reserved (salva ratificatione), as well as the instruction of the commissioners. - The proper activity of the assembly, the business with respect to the constitutional question, had thereby passed over to the committee.

It is now mentioned that meetings of the estates' commissioners with the royal ones have taken place; from 28 April onwards, where a report on these negotiations, but not made known in print, occurs, and from 2. May onwards, where a note of the committee to the commissioners, likewise not printed, is read out, one hears nothing more of this negotiating business until 29 May, where Mr Dr Cotta (VI.
Abt., S. 79) in the name of the estates' commissioners laid before them a royal resolution communicated to them on the same day, concerning six subjects of the constitution of the assembly.
Only from the in many respects remarkable speech of Mr Gleich of Aalen of 23. June (VII.
Abt., S. 81) does one learn something more particular about the spirit and the conduct of the committee.

One sees from it namely that the same [committee] had not entered into any development and work on the matter at all, but had simply set up six points, which, as Mr Gleich rightly remarks, were taken partly from the old Württemberg constitution and partly from the royal charter, fragments of constitutions, as preliminary articles. - The delicate - or rather, senseless - intention of such a course of action is given as being to open the court a convenient path, in order to enter into the wishes of the assembly with good grace. - It is just as remarkable from the speech cited to see that the committee had made a secret of these six points even from the assembly of the estates itself.

It is said in the same place that, after it had become known that several members wanted, out of dissatisfaction with it, to leave the diet, they were given a kind of confidential disclosure. - Above, the character of the muteness which the assembly showed from the very beginning has been remarked upon; but now it was further put by its committee into the condition not of deafness - for deaf is only he who does not hear when something is spoken in his presence -, but into the condition of not hearing, because nothing was spoken before it. - One loses here entirely all conception of what one can have of the destiny and the labours of an assembly of the estates. - It is said in the same speech, which likewise emerges from the protocols, that of the indispensable and the only thing which should have happened, 'no thought was now and nevermore to be given to the discussion of these six articles in the assembly of the estates'. - Thus the assembly had still not come to a subject-matter in its deliberations and to an influential activity upon the constitution.
zh: 等级会议于 4 月 24 日任命了一个由 25 名成员组成的委员会来准备谈判，并任命了四名专员，去与国王为此任命的四位国务顾问谈判；据所能回忆，这四位似乎全是老符腾堡人。
如今似乎已经出现了更切近的着手之处，让人有希望把事情引向实质。
很快就表明：这个委员会把所领受的准备工作理解为对谈判的领导以及对等级议会的谈判专员的训令；它在这个意义上开始了工作，并且事实上撇开等级会议本身、全权接管了谈判。
4 月 28 日，一位成员在等级会议中提出，委员会的处境应当说得更确切一些；对此，委员会中最积极的成员之一、事务文书官博莱先生保证说，委员会不会采取危险的步骤，而在必要之处会与等级会议沟通；谈判中有些事情必须保密。
基于这番保证，等级会议正式把谈判的领导权以及对专员的训令移交委员会，并以等级会议的追认为准（salva ratificatione）。——等级会议本身的活动，即与宪法问题相关的那桩事务，至此便转到了委员会身上。
如今有人提到，等级议会的专员们曾与国王方面的专员会面；从 4 月 28 日起——那里有一份关于这些谈判、但未付印公布的报告——从 5 月 2. 日起——那里宣读了委员会给专员们的一份同样未付印的照会——关于这件谈判事务就再也听不到任何消息，直到 5 月 29 日，在那里科塔博士先生（《文件补编》 VI.
，S. 79）以等级议会专员的名义，把同日传达给他们的一项关于等级会议宪法中六个事项的国王决议呈交上来。
直到来自阿伦的格莱希先生 6 月 23. 日那篇在许多方面都引人注目的演说（「《文件补编》 VII.
，S. 81」）中，人们才了解到关于委员会的精神与举止的更多具体情况。

从中可以看出：委员会根本没有就这件事作任何展开与工作，而径直提出了六点——如格莱希先生正确指出的，这六点一部分取自老符腾堡的宪法，一部分取自王家的宪章——并把那些宪法碎片立为预备条款。——对于这种做法，其微妙——其实更应说是不合理——的意图被说成是要为宫廷开辟一条体面的路子，以便好整以暇地迎合等级会议的愿望。——同样引人注目的是，从所引的演说中可以看出：委员会甚至对等级会议本身也把这一点六个要点当作一个秘密。

在同一处还说到：在传出若干成员出于对此的不满而想离开邦议会之后，他们得到了一种近乎私下的透露。——上面已经指出过等级会议从一开始就表现出的那种沉默的性质；如今委员会又把它置于这样一种状态：不是聋——聋只是听不见有人在他面前说话的人——而是不去听，因为在她面前根本没有说话。——到这里，人们对于等级会议的使命与工作所能有的设想就彻底失去了。——同一篇演说里说到——这从会议记录中同样看得出来——对于那唯一不可省略、本应发生的事，「人们再也、永远不再想到在等级会议中讨论这六条」。——于是，等级会议在它的审议中仍未成为一件有实质内容的事情，在宪法问题上也仍未开展起有分量的工作。

en: One learns the secret of the committee's six preliminary articles, which now constitute the turning point, only from an essay of the estates of 26 June (VIII.

Since they concern real matters, they shall be briefly set out here, together with a statement of that which the king's resolution of 29 May concedes concerning them, and which is of the greatest importance.
zh: 委员会那六个预备条款的秘密——它们如今构成了转折点——人们直到看了等级议会 6 月 26 日的一篇文章才得以知晓（「《文件补编》 VIII.
由于它们涉及真正的实质内容，这里便简要列出，同时说明国王 5 月 29 日的决议就此所许可的内容，以及其中最关紧要之处。

en: The first thing which the commissioners demanded, they very clumsily called self-taxation, with the nearer determination that a prior submission of the state's requirements and of a calculation of the chamber revenues, an inspection of the account of these, an examination of the actual use of the granted monies, and an estates' administration of the land funds should be connected with it. - The king withdrew the restriction of the estates' concurrence made in his constitution and conceded that not only the increase but in general the direct and indirect taxes should be granted by the estates; only from the year 1815 to 1818 should the existing ones remain.

A share in the collecting, however, as well as a treasury under their own direction, he did not concede to the estates; but the most exact inspection into all state revenues and expenditures and a complete control with regard to their use, with the exception of the revenues from the king's patrimonial and demesne property, in which the king declared himself not to be averse to a civil list founded on the demesne property.

Further, a debt-payment authority is to be established, with the attendance of an equal number of estates' deputies as of royal deputies. - No remark is needed on the liberality of these royal concessions.
That in an imperial fief, indeed, but not in a state, the estates can have the administration of the state treasury, has been spoken of above.

That the chambers in France and the parliament in England do not have such an administration is well known, - as likewise that in the former country the Chamber of Deputies appoints deputies from among its members to the amortization fund.

The expression land funds, which the estates' commissioners use instead of state funds, served to designate the right which the land has, since the monies are its own and it may administer them itself. - The former custom of the imperial fief, of opposing government and land, could not find its account in the expression state, in which the old sense of that opposition falls away, and the monies of private persons, insofar as they become taxes, become public monies, belong only to the state.
zh: 专员们所要求的第一件事，被他们很不高明地称作「自行课税」，并附有更具体的规定：预先提交国家的需要以及税务收入的估算、查阅该估算的账目、审查所批准款项的实际用途，并由此连带着由等级议会自行管理土地资金。——国王撤销了他在宪法中所作的对等级议会同意权的限制，并同意：不仅增加税赋，而且一切直接税与间接税都应由等级议会批准；只是从 1815 年到 1818 年，当前的税赋维持不变。
但对于征收的分成以及由他们自己主管的一个国库，国王并不肯让步给等级议会；不过他同意对一切国家收入与支出作最仔细的查阅，并在用途上给予完全的监督——王室的私产与公有领地财产所产生的收益除外；在这一项上，国王声明自己并不反对设立一份以公有领地财产为基础的皇室开支清单。
此外还应设立一个债务清偿机构，出席的等级议会议员与王家议员人数相等。——这些王家让步的宽厚无需评论。
在帝国采邑中等级议会固然可以、但在一个国家中不能掌管国库的管理，这一点上面已经说到。
法国的税务机构、英国的议会并没有这样的管理，这是众所周知的——同样众所周知的是，在前一个国家，众议院从自己的成员中选出议员出任摊还基金。
等级议会的专员们用「土地资金」这个说法代替「国家资金」，是为了标示土地所拥有的权利——因为这些钱本来就是自己的，所以也可以自行管理。——帝国采邑的旧习在于把政府与土地对立起来，因此他们的算计无法落在「国家」这一说法上；在「国家」一词中，那种对立的旧义消失了，而私人所有的钱一旦成为税赋、成为公共资金，就只属于国家。

en: The second demand was the restoration of the church property.
The king granted it entirely; only the formerly separate administration he declined.
zh: 第二项要求是恢复教会财产。
国王完全同意了这一点，只是拒绝了从前的分开管理。

en: The third article was a form of representation in which all classes of subjects should be represented relatively equally. - We have already spoken above more exhaustively about this highly democratic form of representation.

To this quite indeterminate, concealed demand the king replied that he expected further proposals concerning it; this much alone he declared, that he would not enter into a separate representation of the nobility, which apparently was what this was aimed at. - As late as 23. June Mr Gleich says about this point (VII.
Abt., S. 130): 'It is not easy to guess what conception and intention the commissioners had in it.
They should therefore all the more have explained themselves about it in the assembly.
Thus, as late as 23. June, the meaning of this article remained a secret.
zh: 第三条款是一种代表制形式，各等级臣民都应当按比例获得同等的代表。——关于这种十分民主的代表形式，上面已经说得更为详细了。
对于这个完全不确定而隐蔽的要求，国王答复说，他等待关于此事的进一步提案；他只声明了这一点：他不会进入为贵族另设代表制的事情——而这看来正是此处的着眼所在。——格莱希先生直到 6 月 23. 日还在谈这一点（「《文件补编》 VII.
，S. 130）：「专员们对这一条怀有怎样的想法与意图，不容易猜得到。
因此他们本可以在等级会议中就此明确表态——这本也是轻而易举的。
可见直到 6 月 23. 日，这一条款的含义仍然是个秘密。

en: The fourth article was one which might have lain very much at the heart of those members of the estates who could miss the well-known old system of committees: the uninterrupted exercise of the estates' rights by a permanent committee. - The king replied that the time appointed for the committee's annual session in the royal charter, four weeks, could very well be extended and the summoning could be repeated, if the business required it.

By the way, he made the estates aware of the increase in costs. - This latter circumstance was indeed very significant for the old committees; but one could easily have said that it could rather be a quiet reason for the extension, indeed for the uninterrupted duration of the sittings, even if the business did not require it, than against it.

With regard to the old committees, however, this thought would be superfluous insofar as examples are to be found in the brochure cited above at S. 495, Die Verwaltung der württembergischen Landeskasse, showing that the narrower committee, which had the administration of the fund and the right to summon the larger committee, decreed and caused to be paid to the latter monetary compensation for the fact that it had not summoned it; it thus knew how to produce an increase in costs without there being any business and without any sittings being held. - Only quite recently has it become known to the public that the assembly of the estates, whose deliberations are considered here, has cost the state 260,000 fl.

In the printed protocols now before us it is indeed mentioned several times that there was a report on the salaries of the estates' members and other incidental expenses, and that a committee was also active on this; but it remains in the printed protocols always only at these announcements, without the content of the reports or resolutions being given, without any sums anywhere being specified.

This very subject was least of all one which an assembly of the estates could treat with secrecy; on the contrary, if it once accepted payment of money for its work, or at least for its sitting together, it had to give it the fullest publicity.

This article of the royal constitution, though it ignored the others, it had at least accepted usefully. - It is in itself highly disagreeable when members of the estates receive salaries or daily allowances; this is a circumstance of the highest importance, it changes something essential in the character and the position of a representation of the people; it also belongs to those things by which the property interest is of itself given the preponderance in the elections, apart from the fact that otherwise it is most closely bound up with the honour of such an assembly.
Estates which are paid cannot escape the suspicion or the reproach that such a payment, although not for all, yet for many or for some members, is a regard for them.

In the deliberations of this assembly of the estates there is no mention at all of the feeling against the drawing of a salary, or of any prompting of this or of other important subjects, - quite as if it were self-evident that the deputies are paid, at least, as occurs once, that their expenses are reimbursed. - That reproach, if the reporter remembers correctly, has not been absent in public either. - But the most monstrous demand which an assembly of the estates could make was that it should be able to appoint yet another committee with special salaries and with pensions, and, to justify in advance the incapacity and laziness of the members of the committee, should be allowed, as formerly, to add and to confer places of legal counsel.
zh: 第四条款是这样的：对于那些会怀念那套著名的旧委员会制度的等级议会议员来说，它必定是极为关切的——即由一个常设委员会不间断地行使等级议会的权利。——国王答复说：王家文书中给委员会每年开会定下的四周时间完全可以延长，若事务需要，也可以再次召集会议。
此外他还让等级议会注意到费用的增加。——这一情况对旧委员会来说确实十分重要；但人们本可以很容易地说：它与其说是延长会议、乃至让会议不间断举行的反对理由，不如说是一个不声不响的理由——即便事务并不要求如此。

不过就旧委员会而言，这个想法又显得多余：因为在上面 S. 495 所提到的《符腾堡土地资金管理》（Die Verwaltung der württembergischen Landeskasse）这一小册子里可以找到实例——那个较小的委员会掌管着该资金的管理并有召集较大委员会的权利，它却因自己未曾召集对方而对后者作出并令人付给了金钱补偿；这样它就能在没有任何事务、也没有召开任何会议的情况下造成费用增加。——不久之前公众才得知：这里所考察其审议的这个等级会议，已经让国家花费了 260 000 古尔登。
在现有的印刷会议记录中，确实几次提到曾就等级议会议员的薪俸及其他杂费作出报告，也曾有一个委员会为此工作；但在印刷的会议记录里始终只有这些提示，既没有说明报告或决议的内容，也没有任何地方举出数目。
恰恰这一事项最不该由等级会议以保密的方式对待；相反，一旦它为自己的工作、或至少为了集会领取了报酬，就应当以完全的公开把这件事公之于众。
国王宪法的这一条款，尽管它无视了其他各条，却至少是切实地接受了的。——等级议会议员领取薪俸或津贴，这本身就已经极令人不快；这是一个极为重要的情况，它改变了人民代表制的性质与地位中的某种本质东西；它也属于那些使得在选举中财产自动取得优势的事项之列，此外它还与这样一个会议的荣誉最紧密地相连。
等级议会一旦领取报酬，就永远无法免除这样的猜疑或指责：这样一笔款项，虽说不至于对所有成员，却是许多成员、乃至少数几个成员所图谋的一种考虑。

在这个等级会议的审议中，对领取薪俸的抵触情绪、对这个以及其他重要事项的任何提议，全都没有被提及——仿佛议员领取报酬是不言而喻的，至少像出现过一次的那样，他们只是得到费用的补偿。——如果报告人记得不错，那项指责在公开场合也同样没有消失。——然而，一个等级会议所能提出的最离奇的要求，是它还能够任命一个享有特别薪俸与养老金的委员会；甚至，为了预先为委员会成员的无能与懒惰作辩护，它还应当像从前那样，可以增设并授予法务顾问的职位。

en: It is of no avail that the leaders of the estates claimed nothing for the committee, of whose members they appeared to be the most qualified, with regard to the entire position and the right of the former secret treasury.

With the payment of committee members, and above all with the granting of pensions to those who, as it is said in the draft of the Württemberg constitution to be renewed, 'have wholly devoted themselves to the service of the fatherland and have received the determination to reside in Stuttgart (what devotion!), but at the triennial renewal of the committee are not appointed anew', to whom 'on account of the 'sacrifice' made to the fatherland an annual compensation shall be paid until their reappointment', - this would bring back a condition whose abolition would indeed perhaps not be regarded by the committee members themselves, or by those who might expect to be elected to it, as the greatest step towards a free and popular constitution and as the greatest blessing which the modern age has brought, but certainly by the estates and above all by the people. - Of equal or even greater influence is the circumstance that through such a permanent committee the most important thing of all, the assembly of the estates itself, becomes more superfluous.
Legal provisions, on the other hand, are something inadequate when the matter itself brings it about in this way.
Apart from the spirit which must form itself in such a well-paid committee, the history of the old Württemberg estates has furnished sufficient experience on this point.
It is well known how rare assemblies of the estates have been.

What the estates now seemed to regard as their fundamental guarantee, the uninterrupted duration of committees, they would have had to consider - with more reflection, or merely by looking back at that experience nearest to them - rather as an institution which laid the most dangerous snare for their independence and their true existence, namely as the assembly as a whole.
zh: 等级议会的领袖们就委员会一事——他们显得是其中最有资格的成员——并未对旧有秘密国库的全部状况与权利提出要求，这毫无用处。

委员会成员领取薪俸，尤其是向那些人授予养老金——正如在将要重新制定的符腾堡宪法的草案中所说，他们「完全献身于祖国的服务，并且领受了在斯图加特定居的安排（这是何等的献身！）」，但在每三年一次的委员会改选时却不再被重新任命」——对这些人的「由于为祖国所作的『牺牲』，在重新任命之前应当每年付给他们一笔补偿」——这样做就会重新带回一种状态：它的废除，也许委员会成员自己、或者那些有望被选入委员会的人，不会看作走向自由而合乎民心的宪法的最大一步，也不会看作近代所带给的最大福祉；但等级议会、尤其是人民必定会这样看。——具有同样、甚至更大影响的是：这样一个常设委员会使最重要的东西——等级议会本身——变得更加多余。
然而，如果事情本身就是这样带来的，那么法律条文反而是不足的。
暂且撇开在这样一个优厚供职的委员会中必然会形成的那种精神不谈，老符腾堡等级议会的历史在这方面已经提供了足够的经验。
等级会议是何等罕见，这是众所周知的。
等级议会现在似乎当作自己的守护神来看待的东西——委员会的不间断存续——他们本应当更多地思考一下，或者只是回顾一下离他们最近的那段经验，从而把它看作一种为其独立性与真正的存在——即作为全体会议的这种存在——埋下最危险陷阱的制度，而不是别的东西。

en: The fifth preliminary article demanded is the estates' share in legislation since 1806, namely the revision of the ordinances issued since 1806 by a joint royal and lands deputation. - The king reminded the estates of the means which they already have in this regard in the right of petition. - But apart from this, one can see in the fact that this share was demanded only with reference to the ordinances issued since 1806, when the old estates were abolished, either a blind prejudice in favour of the earlier and a blind animosity against the later which proceeded from the king, or at least the desire to show faith in the excellence of the one and dissatisfaction with the other.

Further, the revision, to be carried out merely by a deputation of royal councillors and estates members - for which the popular name 'royal and lands' comes up again -, has been proposed in a stranger and more irregular fashion, whereas the concurrence of the whole assembly of the estates belongs to the business of legislation; for the preparatory work for it, as for all other preparatory work, it had the power to entrust them to committees auf[zu]tragen.
zh: 所要求的第五个预备条款是等级议会对 1806 年以来立法事务的参与，即由王家与等级双方共同的代表团对 1806 年以来所颁布的法令进行审查。——国王提醒等级议会：在这方面他们已经拥有请愿权这一手段。——此外，人们在这件事上——即这种参与仅仅就 1806 年（旧等级议会正是在这一年被扬弃）以来所颁布的法令而提出要求——只能看出：要么是对旧者的一种盲目偏爱和对后来那些出自国王的东西的一种盲目敌意，要么至少是那种想要显示对前者的卓越的信念以及对后者的不满的欲望。
此外，这项审查——按提议它仅仅由一个王家枢臣与等级议会议员组成的代表团来进行——为此那套老套的「王家与等级」的名称又重新冒了出来——被以一种更奇怪、也更不合规矩的方式提了出来；其实，整个等级会议的同意权本来就属于立法事务；而对于其中的前期工作，正如对于其他一切前期工作一样，等级议会有权把它们委托给委员会 auf[zu]tragen。

en: The sixth article is free movement in the old sense of the word. - The king granted it, also before the expiry of a year after the declaration of will of one who would wish to emigrate, as was formerly determined, even in the case of serfdom, without having to buy himself free from it.
But since emigration also concerns a relation to other states, he insisted on the principle of reciprocity with regard to the emigration tax.
zh: 第六条款是旧意义上的自由迁徙。——国王准许了这种自由，甚至在想要移居者作出意志声明后不到一年之内——如先前所规定的那样——也准许，即便在农奴制的情况下，也无需花钱赎身。
但由于移居同时牵涉到与其他国家的关系，他在离境税的问题上坚持互惠原则。

en: The estates' negotiating commissioners had presented these articles with the peremptory declaration that without a contractual recognition of them no happy result of the negotiations was to be hoped for and the cooperation of the estates was in the present emergency absolutely impossible; that they therefore had to request that the king would give a satisfying declaration now, and before anything further was done, and that indeed not only to satisfy the assembly but also the domestic and even the foreign public. - The king, who overlooked both the circumstance that the assembly made its cooperation in the then necessary efforts of the state dependent on the submission of the king to their will, which was to happen at once, and before anything further was done, and such a form of negotiation as beginning with the presentation of disconnected, indeterminate, in part scanty preliminary articles, and who with great indulgence in respect of the material went towards the estates, added, however, that his resolutions rested on unalterable principles, that the negotiation with the estates' deputies should be continued on the same and an agreement should be sought to be brought about.
zh: 等级议会的谈判专员们提交这些条款时附上了一个斩钉截铁的声明：若不以契约方式承认这些条款，谈判就不可能有好的结果，而等级议会的参与在当前的危急之中更是绝对不可能；因此他们必须请求国王现在、在进一步有所行动之前，就作出一个令人满意的声明——而且不仅仅是为了安抚等级会议，也为了安抚国内的、甚至外国的公众。——国王对两件事都不予追究：其一，等级会议把自己对国家当时必需的努力的参与，取决于国王当下、在进一步有所行动之前就要服从他们的意志；其二，谈判以提出彼此不相连贯、不确定、部分内容贫乏的预备条款来开场。同时，国王在实质问题上以极大的宽容相向于等级议会；但他补充说：他的决议立足于不可更改的原则；与等级议会议员的谈判应在这些决议的基础上继续，并应努力达成一项协议。

en: The estates, however, did not continue these negotiations.

Their manner so far, of staying with the demand for the merely formal, could appear justified by the important concessions which they had obtained from the king on this path, if they had now entered into the matter.

Even if the negotiating committee had still wanted to persist in ignoring the royal constitution, by which a part of its articles was partly already settled and partly also better carried out and developed, it was now probably time that the assembly should deliberate, should bring the particular to consciousness and should say what it found acceptable and what not.

From that there would at least have resulted preliminary articles, and indeed of an agreement, not of a submission of the king. - But just as the six articles were not subjected to a discussion of the assembly before, when they were presented for unconditional preliminary acceptance, just as little was this done after the royal declaration upon those articles and upon the content of this declaration had been made.
Against this, three or four members again read essays, namely in the shape of drafts of a reply to the royal resolution.

The fixed idea of the dry principle of restoration of the old constitution founded the naivety that the assembly always found itself outside the matter and that even now it did not trouble itself with this, but only with its own diplomatic manner of how an answer was to be given. - Mr Dr Cotta had on 1. May in the committee read an essay concerning the matter, which particularly concerned the establishment of an estates' fund, which was then brought before the assembly and had as its consequence an essay by Mr Dr Weishaar (sitting of 27 May, Abt. VI, S. 38); later, on 23. June, he had another follow, in which the thought was developed that such a fund, like the other good things of the old constitution in general, was not to be extended to the elements which interfere with the rights of the regents, and that that fund should rather be restricted to what the credit of the state and the dignity of the estates allow.

Much as these thoughts, to which he also returned later, were suited to a thorough deliberation before a resolution on the royal declaration, the consequences were only these: that three weeks later, and at the same time long after the answer to the royal resolutions had been accomplished, Mr Amtsschreiber Bolley, and eight days later again Mr Dr Weishaar, read essays against the ideas of Mr Dr Cotta.

There was no voting on the matter itself at all. - Of what Mr Bolley, as he called it, had written down, and the reading of which, as the protocol states (Abt. IX, S. 114), was taken up by the assembly with lively thanks, this may be picked out: that in it he took into account the well-known work of the state minister von Wangenheim, Idee der Staatsverfassung, and (IX.

Abt., S. 124) does him the justice, 'that the rights of the people, notably of the Württembergers, have found in the noble author such a warm defender'. - It may also be mentioned from this that the author asserts in regard to an estates' disposition over the tax fund (ibid., S. 135), 'if high purposes of state in extraordinary cases demand the speedy raising of monies, the estates, keeping the most important thing in view, will certainly never scruple to support their sovereign to the best of their ability'. - This certainty is very naive; the guarantee for the state should lie in such an assurance, that it would not be dangerous for it to constitute two independent powers of government.
This certainty is all the more naive, since one could ask what purpose of state could be more important, what case more extraordinary, than the moment of Napoleon's reappearance in France?

How, a few weeks before Mr Bolley read his essay and this assurance of his, the Württemberg assembly of the estates supported their sovereign to the best of its ability and joined itself to the cause of Germany and Europe, we have seen.
zh: 然而等级议会并没有继续这些谈判。
他们迄今为止的做法——停留在仅仅形式上的要求上——由于在这条途径上从国王那里取得了重要的让步，若他们现在肯着手处理实质，倒也可以显得是正当的。
即便谈判委员会那时还想坚持无视王家宪法——它的一些条款由此已部分地获得解决，部分地也得到了更好的贯彻与展开——现在大概也是时候了：等级会议应当加以商议，应当把具体内容提高到自觉，应当说出它认为可以接受什么、不能接受什么。
从中至少本可以产生出一些预备条款——而且是通向一项协议、而不是国王屈服的预备条款。——然而，那六条款在被提出来作为无条件的初步接受之前，既未提交等级会议讨论；在国王就那些条款、就这一声明的内容作出声明之后，同样也没有这样做。
与此相对，三四位成员又朗读了文章，即以答复国王决议的草案的形式。

那种把旧宪法的干燥的恢复原则当成固定想法的念头，造成了这样一种天真的做法：等级会议总是处在事情之外；即便现在，它也不是拿事情本身、而是只拿自己那套关于「该如何答复」的外交方式来行事。——科塔博士先生于 5 月 1. 日在委员会里朗读了一篇涉及此事的文章，该文特别关乎设立一个等级议会基金；这篇文章随后被提交给等级会议，并引出了魏斯哈尔博士先生的一篇文章（5 月 27 日会议，《文件补编》 VI, S. 38）；后来，在 6 月 23. 日他又让人读了另一篇，其中展开的思想是：这样一个基金，正如旧宪法中其他一切好的东西一样，不应扩展到那些侵及摄政者权利的成分上去；这个基金反而应当被限制在国家信用与等级议会的尊严所允许的范围内。
这些思想——他后来还再次回到它们上面——本来很适于在就国王的声明作出决议之前加以彻底商议；可是其结果不过是：三个星期之后、同时也在对国王各项决议的答复早已办妥之后很久，事务文书官博莱先生朗读了反对科塔博士先生思想的文章，又过了八天，魏斯哈尔博士先生也朗读了这样的文章。
就事情本身根本没有进行表决。——博莱先生所写的（他称之为）东西——据会议记录所说，等级会议以热烈的感谢接受了对它的朗读（《文件补编》 IX, S. 114）——其中可以摘出这一点：他在其中顾及到了国务大臣冯·旺根海姆先生的著名著作《国家宪法的观念》，并且（《文件补编》 IX.

，S. 124）他对作者公道地说：「人民的权利、特别是符腾堡人的权利，在这位高尚的作者那里找到了一位如此热心的辩护者。」——由此还可以指出：这位作者就等级议会关于税务资金的一项安排断言说（同上，S. 135），「如果国家的高目的在非常情况下要求迅速筹集款项，那么等级议会心里装着最重要的那件事，就肯定不会迟疑，要尽力支持自己的君主」——这种「肯定」实在天真；对国家的保证本应在于这样的保证之中：对它来说，设立两个独立的统治权并不危险。
这一「肯定」就更加天真，因为人们不妨要问：还有哪个国家目的比拿破仑在法国重新出现的关头更重要，还有哪种情况比这更非常呢？
就在博莱先生朗读他的文章与这番保证的前几个星期之前，符腾堡等级会议曾尽力支持自己的君主，并与德国和欧洲的事业合流——这一点我们已经看到过了。

en: A more comprehensive occasion for entering into the articles in question was provided to the assembly by the already several times mentioned, bold, eloquent, excellent in thought and spirit address of Mr Gleich of Aalen of 23. June.

He states expressly that what is at stake for the estates is not the old Württemberg constitution but a good constitution, not an empty formal law but the thing itself, and he takes up, reasonably enough, not a few disconnected fragments but the essential principles on which it depends.
The assembly found itself surprised at a tone so foreign to its fixed ideas, to its eternal self-praise and to the praise of all the newspapers.

That Mr Gleich's courage did not fare well at the hands of the assembly has already been mentioned above; this voice echoed in the desert and it was made clear to him through half a dozen essays that his motion meant to 'enter into the royal resolution and not to discard, as it were, the in part acceptable offers of the king'. - Mr Gleich, however, now disappears from the assembly, without any explanation of his departure emerging from the protocols, and later another representative of Aalen appears.

This, however, belongs in general to the irregularities of the assembly: that members lay down their deputy's office and others step forth in their place, without it being evident from what formal authorization each of the two happens. - With regard to Mr Gleich one reads only, a year and a day later, in a sitting the obscure remark of a member, which warned another deputy, who differed from the opinion of the majority, of the fate which Mr Gleich had had.
zh: 使等级会议着手处理现有这些条款的一个更为全面的契机，是来自阿伦的格莱希先生 6 月 23. 日那篇前面已经几次提到过的、勇敢的、有说服力的、在思想与精神上都极为出色的演说。
他明确说出：等级议会所关涉的不是老符腾堡的宪法，而是一部好的宪法；不是一种空洞的形式法，而是事情本身；并且他合理地把握的不是几个互不相连的碎片，而是那些本质的原则——事情正在于此。
等级会议惊讶于这样一种语调：它与他们那些固定的看法、他们永恒的自我表扬以及所有报纸的赞扬都如此陌生。
格莱希先生的勇气在等级会议方面没有好下场，这一点上面已经提到；这个声音在荒漠中回荡，而且通过半打文章向他表明，他的提案是要「着手处理国王的决议，不要把国王那些部分可以接受的提议就此丢开」。——然而格莱希先生从此时起就从等级会议中消失了，会议记录中并没有对他的离去作出任何说明；后来又出现了一位来自阿伦的代表。
不过，这本身就属于等级会议的一种不合规矩：成员辞去自己的议员职位，而另一些人接替着出站出来，却无从看出这两种情形各自依据何种正式授权而发生。——关于格莱希先生，人们只是在一年零一天以后的一次会议中读到某位成员的晦暗言论：他警告另一位与多数人意见相左的议员，说他将遭遇格莱希先生所遭遇的命运。

en: With the motion of Mr Gleich the assembly rejected the position into which the royal resolutions had opened the way for it, the position of declaring that an agreement on very essential points was present, and thereby of laying a firm basis for further negotiation.

It did not discuss the matters themselves, nor which of the king's resolutions were acceptable in their content and which not, but only such things as which essays it would attach to its reply, what title it would give them, and such formalities, in a few sittings.
On 26 June, four weeks after the receipt of the royal resolution, it had at last finished its reply (VIII.
Abt., S. 58 ff.).
This reply too did not consist in a counter-instruction to their plenipotentiaries, but in an address to the king.
The assembly thus fell back into the old path of its libelling, which had so far led to nothing and for whose sake the path of oral negotiations with royal commissioners was to have taken its place.
zh: 随着格莱希先生的提案，等级会议抛弃了国王的各项决议为它开辟道路的那个立场——即宣布在若干极重要的点上已经存在一项协议的立场——从而也就抛弃了为进一步谈判奠定一个稳固基础的可能。
它没有讨论那些实质内容，也没有讨论国王的各项决定按其内容而言哪些可以接受、哪些不可以接受；在几次会议中，它所讨论的只是：应当在答复中附上哪些文章、该给这些文章加上什么题目，以及这类形式上的事项。
6 月 26 日——在收到国王决定四个星期之后——它终于拟就了自己的答复（「《文件补编》 VIII.
这份答复也不是给其谈判全权代表的一份反指示，而是一封致国王的呈文。
于是等级会议又退回到它那条老路上——那条书面攻讦的老路；这条路迄今没有通向任何东西，而正是为了取代它，本应让与王家专员的口头谈判这条道路接替上来。

en: The address itself is, without touching on the king's indulgence, filled with nothing but the expressions of a complete deception of their hopes, of their nameless pain and astonishment, of their impossibly conscientious conviction, with the self-glorification of their love of truth, of which every unclean motive, every selfish intention is foreign, of the testimony of their conscience before God, before whose judgement seat they will one day be summoned, and suchlike pathos.
With regard to the matter, the answer was quite simply and naively this: that the royal resolution could not be reconciled with the principle of the estates.

The pathetic conclusion of the address is that it asks the king, indeed adjures him, by God, by everything holy and honourable, by the happiness of his own Most Serene Highness's family, that he would no longer refuse the restoration of the former state of law.

Mr Gleich had intermingled no such empty pathos into his address, but developed so much more reason in it - which, however, did not produce the desired effect; perhaps he would have got further with that sort of pathos, but at most he would only have averted the insinuation of dishonest intentions. - Otherwise the ordinary reasons from positive state law and from the contractual relation, but especially, have brought home to the king that he himself, like the earlier regents, on his accession to the government solemnly vowed and swore to maintain the constitution.
They add that they have examined most conscientiously whether a change had occurred which according to principles of law could annul these obligations; they could find no such legal ground.

That they would have had to search more thoroughly, to that they would have had to be urged by the very circumstance that otherwise they saw themselves in the authorization to bring against their prince the charge of perjury towards his whole people, - an authorization and an action before which they would have had to recoil.
zh: 这份呈文本身——不去触动国王的宽容——只是充满了这样的言词：对自身希望的彻底欺骗、一种无名的痛苦与惊愕、一种不可能的良知确信；充满了对其真理之爱的自我夸耀——这种爱是任何卑污的动机、任何自私的意图都与它无缘的；充满了在上帝面前、在上帝的审判席前他们终将受召的良知的证词；以及诸如此类的浮夸。
就事情本身而言，这个答复既简单又天真的内容便是：国王的决议无法与等级议会的原则相调和。
这份呈文那浮夸的结语是：它请求国王，甚至向他起誓——以上帝、以一切神圣而可敬的事物、以他本人至为尊贵家族的幸福起誓——不要再拒绝恢复先前的法权状态。
格莱希先生在他的演说里没有掺入这类空洞的浮夸，反而在其中展开了多得多的理性——只是这理性并没有产生所期望的效果；也许他用那种浮夸反倒能推进一些，但至多不过是避开了「存心不诚」这一暗指的嫌疑罢了。——否则，从实定国家法与契约关系中得出的那些通常的理由，尤其是以下几点，会使国王本人明白：他自己如同先前的统治者那样，在登基即位之时曾庄严地许诺并宣誓要维护这部宪法。
他们补充说：他们曾极其认真地考察过，是否发生过某种变化，按法权根据能够解除这些义务；他们找不到这样一个法权根据。
他们本应当更彻底地查找；促使他们这样做的，恰恰是这一情况：否则他们就会自以为自己有权对他们的君主提出「对其全体人民背誓」的指控——而这样的权力与这样的行为，本应使他们却步。

en: To the address were attached, besides two essays, above all a third appendix, an essay or rather a book in small print of 162 pages (VIII.
Abt., S. 91-252), - namely the so-called presentation of the grievances of the land.
On this book the members had worked for many weeks and had gathered from all sides every kind of grievance.

One has to read it in the deliberations themselves how, with this work, the estates seemed to have done the most important work, to have fulfilled their most sacred duty, to have justified their whole conduct towards the king in the most unanswerable manner.
It is, especially in this announcement, impossible to go into the content of this glaring picture of oppression and complaints.

Apart from the investigation of the factual assertions, it might seem necessary to distinguish what were real and what were supposed grievances; for at the first glance one sees that a quantity of the complaints rests on the judgement of the authors about the usefulness or harmfulness of state institutions.
Then it would be to be distinguished what of the burden of the taxes, insofar as it is founded, falls on the government and what on the necessity and unfavourableness of the times.

One has indeed seen this mixture in all the German lands - discounting the manifold unreasonableness of complaining and of discontent - to attribute to the will of the government what was a consequence of the enormous circumstances and events of the last 25 years.

One sees in this collection of grievances, in this respect too, that the estates lacked knowledge of the needs of the state and the condition of the state treasury, and that the complaints about the imposts were raised without any comparison with the needs of the state.

In special consideration, however, it would have to be examined whether the abolition of the old Württemberg constitution was the sole ground of the well-founded grievances; for this was the most important thought which was to be thereby proved - or rather, not to be proved, but was simply presupposed; still less is it shown that the royal constitution with the further provisions just conceded is not capable of remedying the grievances, and indeed that they must rather continue to exist under it.
This latter point of view, of whose development no thought at all is given, would have been the only nerve of the remonstrance which was to be supported by this mass of grievances.
zh: 除两篇文章之外，主要是又附上了第三份附件：一篇论文，或者不如说是一本小开本的书，共 162 页（「《文件补编》 VIII.
，S. 91-252），——即所谓的《土地陈情的陈述》。
成员们在这本书上花了许多周工夫，从四面八方搜罗来各种各样的陈情。
必须在会议记录本身中去读，才能看出：等级议会如何凭着这项工作自以为做成了最要紧的事、尽到了最神圣的职责，并以最不容反驳的方式为自己对国王的一切行为作了辩护。
尤其在这份提要中，要进入这幅压迫与哀诉的刺目图景的内容是不可能的。
对事实性断言的考察暂且不说，还似乎有必要区分：哪些是实在的陈情，哪些是想像中的陈情；因为人们一眼就看出，有大量的哀诉建立在作者们对国家制度之有用或有害的判断之上。
其次则须区分：赋税负担中，凡是有根据的那一部分，应归于政府；哪一部分则应归于时代的必要与不利。
人们确实在所有德意志邦国都看到了这种混淆——若撇开抱怨与不满的多重不合理不谈——即把本是一切巨大的情势与事件在二十五年间所造成的后果，归到政府的意志上。
在这一陈情汇编中，就这一着眼点而言，人们同样看到：等级议会并不了解国家的需要与国库的状况；而关于各项摊派的哀诉，是在完全不与国家的需要作比较的情况下提出的。
不过就特殊的一层考虑而言，还须考察：老符腾堡宪法的扬弃是否是那些有根据的陈情的唯一缘由；因为这正是那个最高层的想法——它本来要由此得到证明，或者更确切地说，本是根本不该得到证明，而干脆被预设了；至于说国王的宪法连同刚刚让步的那些进一步规定不能解除这些陈情、甚至这些陈情在它之下反而必定继续存在，这一点就更加没有加以论证了。
最后这一着眼点——对它连想都没有想过如何展开——本曾是那项由这堆陈情所支撑的抗议的唯一命脉所在。

en: Such investigations, which might at first show themselves to be just, are in fact altogether superfluous, since this work which seemed so weighty was from the outset afflicted with a fundamental defect and had to remain without important consequences, indeed was even to remain without them. - Here it may be remarked only this much: that the land's gravamina, the cahiers des doléances, were a well-known item in the business of former imperial estates.

Equally well known is how little has ever been achieved with it, how every diet or imperial diet found the preceding mass of grievances for the most part still undecided and sought to swell it further with fresh material, so that this moles itself and the habit become fixed on the one hand of the estates or parliaments, to expatiate in such a far-ranging manner, drawing in everything possible, on complaints and grievances according to duty and conscience, and on the other hand the habit of the governments, to receive along with the concessions of their estates such a moles as well, have made both parties so dulled and hardened against it that the presentation and the reception of these written masses sank to the significance of a formality.

The reporter remembers to have read somewhere that, when in the course of the legal proceedings there between Duke Karl of Württemberg and his estates, in the year 1768, the collection of grievances of the latter was submitted by the imperial supreme court at Vienna to the commissioners of the duke, those commissioners replied in substance that the imperial supreme court should not be surprised at such a mass, since for several hundred years the authors of gravamina had vied with their predecessors in surpassing them in the description, and if one were to credit such amplification the land must have been utterly ruined long since.
zh: 这类考察——它们乍看之下可能显得公正——其实完全是多余的：因为这部看似如此重要的著作从一开始就带着一个根本缺陷，而且必定不会产生重要的后果，甚至本来就应当不产生任何后果。——关于这一点这里只须提一句：土地陈情书、法国的陈情册（cahiers des doléances），是往昔帝国等级议会事务中一项众所周知的议题。

同样众所周知的是：这一套从来就没有取得什么成效；每一次邦议会或帝国议会，多半只是找到上一堆尚未处理的陈情，并且想用新的材料使它继续膨胀；于是这一大堆本身，连同那已经固定下来的习惯——一方面是等级议会或议会习惯于如此铺张地、把一切可能的东西都牵扯进来地、本着职责与良知去铺陈那些哀诉与陈情，另一方面是政府习惯于在批准其等级议会的请求之外还要再收到这样一大堆——已经把双方都磨得对这一切如此麻木、如此坚硬，以至于呈递和接收这些文书大堆都降低成了某种纯粹形式上的意义。
报告人记得曾在什么地方读到过：1768 年，在符腾堡公爵卡尔与其等级议会之间于当地进行的诉讼程序中，后者的陈情汇编由维也纳的帝国最高法院提交给了公爵的专员；这些专员大致答复说，帝国最高法院不应当为这样一大堆而感到惊异——因为几百年来，陈情书的作者们一直竞相要在描述上超越并压过自己的前任；而如果人们真要相信这种膨胀描写的分量的话，那片土地早就该被彻底毁掉了。

en: The Württemberg assembly of the estates, for which the royal constitution had opened up a quite different path, the path not merely of gravaminating but of working at the removal of the defects, preferred - since it had run aground in its principle of law in old-constitutional procedure - merely to take the accustomed path, to travel the old high road, and to collect the mass of quarrels.
For it would have gone against its conscience to contribute to the remedy itself, because it would have believed that by a work in deed it was thereby recognizing the royal constitution in fact.

It is also an easier work to drag together such a mass of grievances than to devise and work out constitutional and legislative arrangements, by which alone a thorough remedy is effected, by which alone a remedy can be effected; it is easier to puff oneself up on the first way merely to a hollow feeling of the discharge of duty and of false satisfaction of conscience, than to acquire on the second way a more laborious but at the same time more modest and more real merit.

A pressure such as that which arose from the excessive rearing of game and from the hunts, and which seems to have been hard enough, is well qualified to be disposed of by mere complaint; for the remedy requires nothing further than a royal command to shoot the game on the head; - and it emerges from the deliberations that the king, on the first representations of the estates on this matter, had already in March (II.

Abt., S. 57) given orders to check this evil, 'as the disposal of it depended in the first instance on him'; when the estates later had doubts about the sufficient efficacy of these orders, they rightly renewed their representations.

But in reckoning up along with those evils everything else which seemed to them unjust and harmful in the state institutions and the state economy, and in dealing with it likewise by complaining and lodging grievances, it looked as if they also imagined the remedy of these evils in such a way that the king only needed to give the order to have them shot away.
zh: 符腾堡等级会议本有一条完全不同的路可走——王室宪法为它开辟的那条路，即不只是去递送陈情书、而是去着手消除那些弊端的道路；但它在法权原则上已经卡在旧式宪法程序的死胡同里，于是宁可只走那条习惯的老路、那条旧大道，去收拢一大堆纠纷不满。
因为它会认为这就违背了自己的良心：单靠实际行动去促成补救，就等于事实上承认了王家的宪法。
把这样一大堆陈情搜罗起来，毕竟比构思并制定宪章与立法上的安排要容易；只有后者才能从根本上加以补救，也只有后者才可能加以补救。用前一种方式把自己撑大，只换得一种空荡荡的尽责感和虚假的良心满足，这比用第二种方式去赢得一种更费力、但同时也更朴实、也更实在的功绩，要容易得多。
像因过度豢养野味与围猎而产生的那种压迫——它看上去已经足够沉重——大概完全有资格用单纯的抱怨来打发了；因为补救所需要的无非是一道王家的命令：把野味就地击毙；——而且从会议记录可以看出，在等级议会就此提出的最初几次陈情之后，国王早在 3 月（《文件补编》 II.
，S. 57）就已经下达命令来制止这种弊害——「因为这件事的处置首先取决于他」；后来等级议会对这些命令是否足够有效产生了怀疑，他们理应重新提出自己的陈情。
他们把一切其他在他们看来于国家制度与国家财政而言不公而有害的东西，也同那些弊害一股脑儿地数算进来，并且同样以抱怨与陈情来应付；这样看起来，他们对消除这些弊害的设想也是：国王只需下一道命令，把它们清除掉就是了。

en: Now all merit may perhaps not be denied to that combining together of defects and mischief; but it only makes the want of the second merit, of really contributing to the remedy by well-considered proposals for remedial laws, all the more striking.

Only in a preliminary deliberation on the essays mentioned - of 26 June (Abt. VIII, S. 8) - is there voiced the neat scruple that the ministry might enter into the essay on grievances, - that is to say, it might divert from the main thing, i.e. the restoration of the old Württemberg constitution, to that.
Count von Waldek had therefore proposed along with this doubt at the same time a turn in the address, by which one might secure oneself against the entering into it.

This turn and reservation was then given by Mr Bolley, in the following words: 'that the estates will not allow themselves to be diverted, through negotiations about individual grievances, from the achievement of their higher purpose, their only concern, but yet have a sacred duty to fulfil by the presentation of the grievances'. - If it was to be through negotiations that the grievances were to be treated, then these gave ample material for years-long or rather endless negotiations, since no imperial supreme court existed any longer for their conclusion.

But if the estates wanted to enter neither into legislative work nor into so-called negotiations, thus into nothing at all, what use was that ballast of grievances? - Was it to be left to the ministry henceforth to remedy them in its own way? - In truth this ballast served for nothing else than that the estates, as they say, had fulfilled a sacred duty; the holier but admittedly more sour duty, of making a beginning with the remedy through legislative work, was not even mentioned.

The king gave on 21. July (X. Abt., S. 14) the only possible decision: that he would have to be put in a position, through the reports of his ministries, to give his decision on the grievances presented.
zh: 这样一来，把种种缺陷与弊害凑拢到一处的做法，大抵也不能说它毫无功绩；但这只会使得第二种功绩的缺失——即通过经过深思熟虑的补救性法律提案真正促成补救——显得更加突出。
不过在关于所提那些文章的一次预先审议中——6 月 26 日（《文件补编》 VIII, S. 8）——竟提出了一种漂亮的顾虑：各部不妨去接手那篇陈情文章；——也就是说，各部想把人们的注意力从主要之事、即恢复老符腾堡宪法这件事上引开。
瓦尔德克伯爵因此在这个疑问的同时，提议在呈文中加一个转折，使人们可以防着自己被拉进去。
这个转折与保留随后由博莱先生提出，他这样措辞：「等级议会不会因为就个别陈情进行谈判而让自己的更高目的——他们唯一关切的目的——受到妨碍；但他们仍负有通过呈递这些陈情来履行一项神圣义务。」——如果这些陈情竟然要通过谈判来处理，那么它们自然为旷日持久的、毋宁说是无休止的谈判提供了充分的材料，因为已经不再有一个帝国最高法院来结束这些谈判了。
可是，如果等级议会既不从事立法工作，也不去从事那种所谓的谈判——总之是一概不沾——那么这一大堆陈情又派什么用场？——难道就任凭各部此后用他们自己的方式去补救吗？——事实上，这一大堆陈情除了让等级议会——按他们自己的说法——履行了一项神圣义务之外，别无用处；那更神圣、但也无疑更酸的义务——通过立法工作开创补救的开端——则根本未被提及。
国王于 7 月 21. 日（《文件补编》 X, S. 14）给出了唯一可能的答复：他必须先通过各部呈递的报告而处于能够对所提出的陈情作出决断的地位。

en: Among the mass of grievances, however, one concerns in passing that which has been called the absurdity of the scribal business.

Through the tireless reminders of Mr von Forstner, this subject has been lifted out of 'the melancholy litany of grievances' and brought to a more detailed examination, which makes the public acquainted with an institution quite peculiar to Württemberg, the scribal institution, and discloses a condition of legal and moral as well as intellectual rot, which among other things gives an account of an important moment, the interest in the good old law, and on account of its far-reaching influence deserves to be examined more closely.
zh: 然而在这一大堆陈情之中，有一条顺带涉及那被称作文书吏之弊的事情。
通过冯·福斯特纳先生不知疲倦的提醒，这一题材被从「陈情的忧郁祷文」中解救出来，并得到了更为详尽的考察；这一考察使公众认识到符腾堡所特有的一个机构——文书吏衙门——并揭示出一种法权上的与道德上的、以及同样在智识上的败坏状态；这种状态除别的之外还使人得以看清一个重要的关节点——即对良好旧法的利益——而由于它影响深远，值得更仔细地考察。

en: As early as 15 May Mr von Forstner presented the influence which the so-called scribal men have on state administration as a general plague of the land, and he expressed it that it is the former Württemberg estates' constitution in whose very core this evil is rooted, which grants to the scribal men 'a wide field for arbitrariness, oppression and pocketing' (Abt. V, S. 58).
A committee was now set up to draw up a report with proposals for the improvement of the institution.

When in the course of six weeks this subject did not come up, Mr von Forstner repeated his motion on 28 June; he remarked in doing so that, though the absurdity is an abomination to many an estimable principal of scribal men, such a man cannot prevent it and can only wish for a reform in secret, because he does not dare lay hands on the sanctuary of the old constitution, knowing that this evil is founded deep in it and is most intimately interwoven with it.

He adds that the Württemberger will never feel relieved in his fate (that is, not even after the restoration of the old constitution - on the contrary), as long as this evil is not removed; that this is intolerable and more than enough to drive the common man to despair.

He adduces as fact and from unimpeachable testimony that this evil has at all times caused the so frequent emigrations of the old Württembergers abroad - emigrations which have taken place both at the height of the former estates' constitution and in the reigns of the most diverse Württemberg rulers.
What, he further exclaims, could have moved [them] to this other than the constitution?
What expressed itself in it so intolerably?
What did it bring to despair under this constitution?
Nothing other than the pressure of the scribal estate.

And it was the constitution which authorized this estate to vex the subject, etc. - In further renewal of his motion (Abt. XVI, S. 84) he cites from the report of a former Württemberg president of the government von Gemmingen a passage in which it is said that 'Württemberg has the sad distinction before other lands of nourishing a peculiar race of men, which is no longer known in the rest of Germany since the time of Dr Faust, - the scribal men.

This race', the text continues, 'is all the more troublesome to the industrious part of the people, since it is at once unashamed and ignoble, claiming at a favourable opportunity to make claims on the first offices of the state, or, at an unfavourable one, to deprive the last class of the people of its sustenance, in all cases always living on the labour of others'. - In a highly remarkable, detailed representation of the Oberamt Horb (XIX.

Abt., S. 26 ff.) one reads that what is drawn annually from scribal earnings amounts on average to more than one annual tax, and in further documentary data one reads that it amounts to six to seven annual taxes.
zh: 早在 5 月 15 日，冯·福斯特纳先生就把那些所谓的文书吏对国家行政的影响描述为一种普遍的灾祸；他并且明言：这一弊害正是植根于旧符腾堡等级议会宪法的最内核之中——正是这部宪法给了文书吏「一片任意的、压迫与搜刮的广阔场地」（《文件补编》 V, S. 58）。
于是设立了一个委员会，起草一份报告并附上改进这一机构的提案。
当这一题材在六个星期内都没有被提及时，冯·福斯特纳先生于 6 月 28 日重申了他的提案；他在重申时指出：这一荒唐事对许多可敬的文书吏头目来说固然是一件令人发指的事，但这样的人无法阻止它，只能在暗中盼望一场改革，因为他不敢触碰旧宪法的圣所——他明知这一弊害深深扎根于其中，并且与它最紧密地交织在一起。
他补充说：只要这一弊害没有被消除，符腾堡人就绝不会在自己的命运中感到轻松——即便旧宪法得到恢复也不会（恰恰相反）；这一弊害令人无法忍受，而且完全足以把普通百姓逼入绝望。
他以事实、并以无可辩驳的证词指出：这一弊害在任何时候都造成了老符腾堡人频繁移居国外——这些移居既发生在旧等级议会宪法最兴盛的时期，也发生在符腾堡历代不同统治者的统治时期。
他进一步呼喊道：除了宪法之外，还有什么能够使[他们]这样做呢？
那里面究竟有什么以如此令人难以忍受的方式表现了出来呢？
在这部宪法之下，它使他们陷入了怎样的绝望之中呢？
除了文书吏这一阶层的压迫之外，别无其他。
而正是这部宪法赋予了这一阶层权利，让它去刁难臣民，等等。——他在进一步重申提案时（《文件补编》 XVI, S. 84），从符腾堡前政府总理格明根大人的报告中引述了一处，其中说：「符腾堡在诸国之中有一项可悲的优先——它养活着一种特有的人种，而在德国其他地方，自 Faust 博士的时代以来就再也见不到了——那就是文书吏。」
「这一类人」，文本继续写道，「对人民中勤劳的那一部分就越加令人厌恶，因为它既厚颜无耻又卑鄙下流：一有有利机会就敢对国家最显赫的职位提出要求，一遇不利机会就从人民的最底层夺去其生计，无论在何种情形下，它总是靠别人的劳动为生」。——在一份极其值得注意的、来自霍尔布上级行政区的详尽呈递中（《文件补编》 XIX.
，S. 26 ff.）人们读到：每年从文书吏的进项中取得的数额，平均超过一份年度税额；而在进一步的文件记载中人们读到，它竟相当于六到七份年度税额。

en: Such a presentation was, to be sure, very contrasting with the tone of the assembly, which always spoke of the three-hundred-year happiness of Württemberg under and through its former assembly of the estates, and with the assurance that the restoration of it was the quite simple remedy for the grievances just brought together, whereas the total mass of these would rather have to seem to be outweighed by this single plague.

Still more contrasting can one find that presentation with the zeal of the assembly for the old law: of its members a part were themselves, and among them such leading figures as Mr Bolley, principals in the writing dynasty; and most of the other deputies, according to their estate, could be brothers, sons or other relatives in this class, or could for their sons and relatives have the right to a share in the advantages of this 'plague'.
The assembly, however, had entered into this subject and had appointed a committee for it, as stated.
But one will wonder - or, if one will, one will not wonder - when one sees the sluggishness with which this subject was treated.
On the second motion of Mr von Forstner too, there was only an exhortation to the committee to hasten its work.

After the assembly, which had adjourned on 27 July, met again on 16 October, nothing further became known about this matter; Mr von Forstner did not desist, but revived the subject again on 5 December; other newly Württemberg deputies added their voices.
zh: 不过，这样一种陈述与等级会议的语气恰恰形成强烈对照：他们总是谈论符腾堡在其旧有等级会议之下、并通过它而享有的三百年幸福，并且断言，恢复这个会议不过是刚刚汇集起来的那些陈情的最简单的补救办法，而陈情的总量毋宁说必定显得要被这一桩单独的灾祸所压倒。
更显对照的是那一陈述与等级会议维护旧法的热忱：这批议员中有一部分本身就是文书吏世家的人，其中就有博莱先生这样的头目；而其余大多数议员按其阶层而言，要么是这一阶层的兄弟、儿子或其他亲属，要么能为其儿子与亲属谋得分享这一「灾祸」好处的权利。
然而，等级会议已经着手处理这个题材，并如前所述为此任命了一个委员会。
不过人们看到这一题材被处理时的拖沓劲儿，会感到惊讶——或者，如果人们愿意，也可以说并不惊讶。
对福斯特纳先生的第二次提案，所得到的也不过是委员会加快工作的敦促而已。
等级会议于 7 月 27 日休会，10 月 16 日再次集会，此后关于这件事就再没有什么消息；福斯特纳先生不肯罢休，于 12 月 5 日又重新把这一题材提了出来；另一些新符腾堡议员也随声附和。

en: When a representation from two office clerks, against one of whom very pressing complaints were received shortly afterwards (Abt. XIX, S. 27), asks the assembly for an improvement in the maintenance of this estate, which, as they assure, by its institution has had for centuries the most beneficent influence upon the state and its members before other lands (Abt. XVIII, S. 27), - then against this, other petitions which kept coming in, many of which remained unprinted, and indeed as the general voice of New Württemberg (Abt. XVIII, S. 95 ff.), stated that if one speaks of the land's grievances and oppressions, this evil must be named first, - they added the proofs which sufficiently established this, 'that the assembly should be intent upon institutions by which the scribal estate should no longer need to brood day and night on defrauding the citizen and on founding its prosperity on the ruin of the subject'.
In all these representations the most glaring facts are cited and the strongest expressions against this oppression are used.
zh: 当一份由两名事务文书官联名的呈递——针对其中一人，紧接着就收到了极为严厉的投诉（《文件补编》 XIX, S. 27）——请求等级议会改善这一阶层的处境时，他们宣称：这一阶层凭借自己的制度，几百年来对国家及其成员的影响比别的国家都更有益（《文件补编》 XVIII, S. 27）；——而与此相对，另一些不断涌入的请愿书——其中许多并未付印，而且是作为新符腾堡的普遍声音提出的（《文件补编》 XVIII, S. 95 ff.）——却说：若谈土地的陈情与压迫，这一件弊害必须第一个被点出来；——他们还附上了足以充分证实这一点的证据：「等级议会应当去谋求这样的安排，使文书吏这一阶层不必再日日夜夜地绞尽脑汁去盘剥公民，把自己的发达建立在臣民的毁灭之上。」
在所有这些呈递中，最刺眼的事实被列举出来，最激烈的措辞被用来控诉这种压迫。

en: Around the time when these pleas for help against this bleeding, this extortion and this swindling came in, the carrying on of remonstrances against a royal tax-execution rescript of the middle of January 1816 concerning the annual tax of 1815/16 was a principal occupation of the assembly of the estates.

The complaints about the intolerable plague and plunder practised by the scribal institution and driving them to despair and the zeal of the estates for a mitigation of the imposts on the state run parallel to one another; so that the compilation turns out as if the collection of the taxes for the purposes of the state were an obstacle to the scribal institution, and as if the latter were hindering the collecting of the annual taxes which it imposed on the subjects.
zh: 大约就在这些求援于救济、以抵制这套盘剥、勒索与诈骗的请求纷纷送到的时候，抗议 1816 年 1 月中旬一道关于 1815/16 年度税赋的王家税收执行敕令，便成了等级会议的一项主要事务。
针对文书吏衙门那套令人无法忍受、把人逼向绝望的灾祸与掠夺的控诉，同等级议会要求减轻对国家负担的税赋的热忱，彼此平行；而汇编出来的结果，看上去就像是：为国家用途而征收税赋，反倒成了文书吏衙门的障碍，仿佛是它在阻挠征收它强加给臣民的那些年度税赋似的。

en: On 24 April 1816, when for almost a year nothing whatever had been done in this matter, Mr von Forstner once more renewed his reminder of it to the assembly in an essay (not printed).

Finally, after more than a year (in which the assembly had needed only a few weeks for the dragging together of its complaints extending to all the branches of the state service), the actual report of the committee established for the absurdity of the scribal estate and of the referent commissioned with it, in which the compilation of these complaints had been announced, has not come into being at all and has not appeared (XXII.
Abt., S. 7, XXV.
Abt. Anh., S. 54).
What has appeared is an opinion of the legal counsellor Griesinger, which has been printed off separately as an appendix to the 25th section, on 192 pages.
This has been read on, piece by piece, from 11. June in several sittings, as opportunity offered, up to 15 July.

Then, apart from a remark of Mr Dr Weishaar on 6 August against a motion made in the previous sitting to actually carry out a reform of the scribal business - of which motion, however, nothing is found in the protocol of the previous sitting - and apart from some other quite isolated remarks, nothing more was done by the assembly in this important matter until shortly before its close.
zh: 1816 年 4 月 24 日——这件事已经将近一年始终没有任何进展——福斯特纳先生又在一篇（未付印的）文章里，向等级会议重申了他对此的提醒。
终于，在一年多以后（在这一年里，等级会议只用了几个星期就把那些伸展到国家行政各个分支的陈情搜罗到了一起），那个为文书吏之弊而设的委员会以及受托办理此事的报告人的正式报告——本来在其中预告要汇编这些陈情——却根本没有产生、根本没有出现（《文件补编》 XXII.
，《文件补编》 S. 7, XXV.
《文件补编》附录, S. 54）。
真正出现的，是法务顾问格里辛格的一份评估意见，它作为第 25 分册的附录单独印行，共 192 页。
这份意见从 6 月 11. 日起，在几次会议中分节陆续宣读，一直到 7 月 15 日才读完。
此后，除了魏斯哈尔博士先生 6 月 8 日针对前一次会议上提出的一项动议——要求真正着手改革文书吏的业务——所作的一点意见之外（而在前一次会议的记录里却找不到这项动议的踪影），以及另外一些完全零星的意见之外，等级会议在这件重要事务上直到临近闭幕都没有再做过什么。

en: The voluminous opinion of the legal counsellor Griesinger states at the very outset that the author refrains from painting the sad picture of all 'the screaming and almost unbelievable facts which have piled up in the petitions and essays on the scribal institution received by the estates, because another member has undertaken this work' - a work which, as has been said, has not been brought to light.

But that opinion, together with the few printed petitions, still contains enough that from it the in fact 'extraordinary and almost unbelievable' nature of this so famous Württemberg institution and its relation to the estates' constitution can become more evident.

Since the author first goes to work historically, he comes, the office of the court clerks being very old, to speak of the old Württemberg courts and to give his view and judgement of them, of which the reporter cannot refrain from picking out some things in the first place, before he comes to the scribal business itself.

century, the following from the Chronogr. gener. about the constitution of these courts:
zh: 法务顾问格里辛格那份冗长的意见一开始就说明：作者不去描绘那幅悲惨的图景——「那些在等级议会收到的、关于文书吏衙门的请愿书与文章中堆积起来的、触目惊心而几乎难以置信的事实」，因为另一位成员已承担了这项工作——而这项工作，正如已经说过的，并没有被公之于众。
不过，那份意见连同少数几份付印的请愿书，所含的内容仍然足够多，以致从中可以更清楚地看出这个如此著名的符腾堡机构的、实际上是「非同寻常而几乎难以置信的」性质，以及它与等级议会宪法之间的关系。
由于作者首先是从历史入手，他——法庭文书吏这一职务既然十分古老——谈到了旧符腾堡的各法院，并对它们提出自己的看法与评判；报告人不免要先从中摘出几点来说一说，然后他才谈到文书吏衙门本身。
作者引证诺克拉大臣的话131)，这位大臣生活在 15 世纪末——
——他引《Chronogr. gener.》中关于这些法院的制度的一段话如下：

en: In every town, market-town and village twelve men, distinguished by integrity of life and honesty, are chosen as judges, without any regard being had to whether they know letters; and those who necessarily undertake the office of judge, even though they have no remuneration or payment at all, do so for the sake of honour.

But for the common good, setting aside their own business, on the appointed days they apply themselves to judging, and each one swears to do what has seemed to him most just and best, and in the presence of the magistrate of the place they hear the causes, and the parties having been heard to satisfaction, they pronounce sentence, not as the laws determine (namely, as it has been said above - the laws of the emperors), of which they have no knowledge whatever, but according as reason and the custom of the courts dictate.132) - But if reason and the custom of the courts, the customary law, the coutumes, contain no laws? - The introduction of the foreign laws also introduced learned legal counsellors into the courts, and this habit finally brought down to nullity those courts consisting of men of equal birth and of outstanding legal integrity, who administered justice not for money but for honour, whose abolition has latterly even been considered necessary.
zh: 「In singulis urbibus, oppidis et villis duodecim viri, vitae integritate ac honestate praecipui, eliguntur in iudices, nullo habito respectu, an sciant literas, nec non, qui munus iudicum necessario subeunt, licet remunerationem seu mercedem nullam habeant, propter honorem.」（在每一座城市、集镇与村庄中，选出十二位以生活端正与诚实著称的人为法官，全不考虑他们是否识字；凡不得不担当法官职务的人，虽则毫无任何报酬与酬金，也只是为了荣誉。）

「Sed pro bono communi, suis posthabitis negotiis, statutis diebus iudiciis intendunt, iurantque singuli, se facturos secundum quod eis visum fuerit iustius ac melius, et praesente magistratu loci causas audiunt, partibusque ad satietatem auditis sententiam dicunt, non ut leges censent (nämlich wie es vorher heißt -leges imperatorum), quorum nullam notitiam habent, sed prouti ratio et consuetudo iudiciorum dictat.」（为了公共利益，他们撇下自己的事务，在规定的日子里专心于审判；每个人都宣誓要去做在他看来最为公正、最为妥当的事，并在当地长官在场时听取案件，在各方陈词已尽之后宣判；他们判案不是按照法令的规定（也就是前面所说的——皇帝的法令），因为他们对这些法令毫无所知，而是按照理性与法院惯例所指示的。）132)——可是，如果理性与法院的惯例、也就是不成文法、那些 coutumes（地方习惯法）并不包含任何法令呢？——外来法制的引入，也把博学的法务顾问带进了各法院；而这一习惯最终把那些由出身相当、法治品格卓越、不为金钱而为荣誉而主持司法的人所组成的法院，降低到一文不值的地步，以致后来甚至有人认为取消它们是必要的。」

en: That fine representation of Naucler the author, however, calls a picture of the ignorance of the Württemberg courts of the time painted in the liveliest colours, and continues from himself: 'In courts where judges sat as has just been described, and who were likewise entirely ignorant of the many (many certainly!) reasonable extensions and restrictions of the laws, the multitude of which nowadays all non-jurists' (as the members of the juries in England and France still are, - an institution which in these countries is regarded as the palladium of freedom) 'are incapable of deciding tangled legal disputes - in such courts the main business of the court clerks could consist only in writing down the silly and tasteless judgments of ignorant judges of a barbaric age.' - One sees that from such views of a legal member of a German assembly of the estates the revival of glorious German antiquities, of genuinely national institutions, is not to be expected.
zh: 不过，作者把诺克拉那幅漂亮的描绘称作一幅以最鲜明的色彩画出的、关于当时符腾堡法院之无知的图景，并自顾自地继续说：「在那些由正如刚才所描述的法官坐镇的法院里——这些法官同样完全不知道法律那许多（有那么多！）合乎理性的扩张与限制，而今天所有非法律人士（英国与法国的陪审团成员至今仍是这种人——在这些国家里，这一制度被看作自由的守护神）——都无法裁断纠缠不清的诉讼——在这样的法院里，法庭文书吏的主要工作只能是抄写那些野蛮时代里不学无识的法官作出的愚蠢而荒唐的判决。」——人们看得出来，从一个德国等级会议的法律专业议员抱着这样的看法，是不能指望重建那些光辉的德国古老习俗与真正属于国家的制度的。

en: The triumph of the new law, 'of the new and bold Ulpians, and the defeats of the Württemberg judges' is carried out further on S. 31: 'The old German law and the old German customs', it says, 'cannot of course be compared with the Roman law; the folly of the raw and uncultured heads of a darker age must form a strange contrast beside the wisdom of the greatest and most sublime jurists of ancient Rome and of the whole world, yes, become utterly ridiculous and contemptible' etc.
Is this the spirit of German popular character which we see honoured and alive in such a tone?

It is further stated with mockery that the diet of the year 1515 and several following ones brought bitter complaints about the learned men, who broke in with their doings noticeably at all the courts throughout the land, so that now one who is in need of justice cannot get away with ten gulden, whereas perhaps twelve years ago he would have settled the matter with ten shillings quite easily; and if no improvement were made here, then in time one would have to appoint to every village one or two doctors who should pronounce law.
Complaints in vain, for 'death has once sworn itself to the old German customs'.

One or two doctors, to be sure, did not come into every Württemberg village, but the scribal men did instead; and it would be useless to examine whether the citizens have gained by these too, which are likewise not old German customs.
zh: 新法的凯旋——「新的、有胆识的乌尔比安们与符腾堡法官们的败绩」——在 S. 31 上还有进一步的铺陈：那里说：「古老的德意志法与古老的德意志习惯，自然而然是无法与罗马法相提并论的；一个更阴暗时代的粗野而未开化的头脑之荒谬，与古代罗马乃至全世界最伟大、最崇高的法学家的智慧并置时，必定构成一种奇特的对照，甚至变得完全可笑、可鄙。」等等。
我们在这个语调里看到它受到尊崇、并且生气勃勃地活着——这就是德意志的民性精神吗？
此外还以嘲笑的口吻指出：1515 年的邦议会以及其后几次，都曾就那些学者提出过激烈的抱怨——这些学者以自己的作为在整个国度的所有法院里明显地横冲直撞，以至于如今一个依法应当得到救济的人，得十个古尔登都难以脱身，而十二年前他也许十个先令就能把这事了结；如果这里再不有所改观，那么久而久之就得在每个村庄里设置一两个博士，由他们来断案。
抱怨是徒然的，因为「死亡早已立誓效忠于那些古老的德意志习惯」。
一两个博士固然没有进入每一个符腾堡村庄，进去的倒是文书吏；至于公民是否也从这些同样并非古老德意志习惯的制度中得了好处，那是没有必要去考察的。

en: These scribal men, then, about whom it is really a question here, the legal counsellor Griesinger defines as legal and cameralistic practitioners, and sets the peculiarity of the Württemberg scribal men in the fact that they are such merely untrained practitioners.

But that this is the case in other lands too, namely to a certain extent, is a known and natural thing, since for a large part of the scribal functions a university education is at least something superfluous.
But according to this opinion and the petitions, the peculiarity of the Württemberg scribal institution shows itself to lie in something quite different.

It emerges from this namely that for every administrative district there is a city or office clerk (for the larger towns, namely, also a special town clerk, and then for the remaining district, which is called the Amt, again a special office clerk), who has the monopoly of having written everything in this district that is to be reckoned and written as judicial and official business. - That the Oberämter, namely the justice and police offices, the cameral administrations, the forest offices, likewise had scribal men as assistants is a circumstance necessary for their business in other countries as well.

In this respect only this can be regarded as peculiar to Württemberg: that among such assistants there are none taken from the class of university-trained jurists, cameralists or foresters, but that all assistants qualify themselves only by routine and are not destined ever themselves to hold an office in whose business they work.
The possession of the forest offices has long ago passed to the nobility; the citizen's assistant is thereby already excluded from the capacity to aspire to such an office.

With regard to the university-trained jurists, it is not the case that it has been made a condition of their being appointed in an office that, after completing their university studies, they acquire the practical skill for this through a practice of one or several years with an official - a preparation which in other states is a statutory requirement.
In the opinion it is mentioned repeatedly that the university-trained jurists consider themselves far too distinguished to enter as assistants with an official.
zh: 这些文书吏——这里真正要谈的就是他们——被法务顾问格里辛格界定为法律与官房方面的实务者；而符腾堡文书吏的特殊之处就在于，他们是这样的、纯粹未经学术训练的实务者。
不过在别的国家、也就是说在某种程度上也是同样情形，这是一件众所周知而自然的事，因为对于文书吏职务中很大一部分来说，大学教育至少是多余的。
但依这份意见与这些请愿书，符腾堡文书吏衙门的特殊之处则显现在完全不同的另一件事上。
从中可以看出：每一个行政区内都设有一名城市或事务文书官（在较大的城市里另有一名专职的城市文书官；其余那个称作「事务区」的区，则另有一名专职的事务文书官），他拥有一种垄断权：这个区内一切属于司法与行政、须要计算与书写的事情，都得由他去让人书写。——至于那些上级行政区，也就是司法与警察局、官房行政机关、林业官署，同样有文书吏充当助手，这是在别的国家里同样为其事务所必需的情形。
就这一点而言，只有下面这一点可以看作符腾堡所特有的：在这样的助手中，没有一个是从受过大学教育的法学家、官房学家或林业官员这一阶层中选出来的；所有助手都只靠日常经验造就，而且并不指望有朝一日自己去担任那个他们现在正为之办事的官职。
林业官署早已被贵族把持；平民出身的助手因此早就被排除在企求这样一个官职的可能之外了。
至于受过大学教育的法学家，则并非规定：他们要在一个官署任职，就得先完成大学学业，再通过在一名官员身边一两年的实务而获得这方面的实际本领——这种准备在别的国家里是一项法定要求。
那份意见里屡次提到：受过大学教育的法学家自视甚高，不屑于到一名官员手下当助手。

en: A petition from the town of Urach, submitted to the assembly of the estates, contains the complaint that the district - excessively large - of the Oberamt which formerly had its seat there had been reduced; among other things the neat thought is expressed that the former many smaller Oberämter had had the use of serving the university-trained jurists, inexperienced in business, as a preparation for their training, - for what? for the administration of more extensive Oberamts districts!
As if the difference did not consist merely in the quantity of business; as far as quality goes they are the same.

According to that idea, the citizens belonging to the smaller administrative districts would be the animae viles of those with whom the inexperienced official was to form himself into an official, merely because they belonged to a geographically smaller district. - Since now that juridical practice which elsewhere is provided to university-trained jurists as a preparation for an office, under the supervision and guidance of a real official, falls entirely to the scribal men, the importance of the latter becomes evident both in relation to an inexperienced superior and in itself, since the university-trained head of an office of 20,000 and more souls, who also combines the police power and branches of the administrative authority with the judicial in himself, has only scribal men as assistants.
zh: 一份向等级会议提交的、乌拉赫城的请愿书里提出这样的控诉：那个从前设在此处、且辖境（过于庞大）的上级行政区被缩小了；请愿书中还表达了一个漂亮的想法：从前那许多较小的上级行政区，本可以让在事务上毫无经验的、受过大学教育的法学家当作练手的场所——用来做什么呢？用来管辖更大的上级行政区辖区！
仿佛差别不在于事务的多少似的；就性质而言，它们是一样的。
